metadata.author: V2 expansion (subagent draft)
metadata.key_test: Fusion under LOW P1: merging two low-capacity, rent-competing states (North Yemen/YAR + South Yemen/PDRY -> Republic of Yemen, 1990) predicts violent dissolution - the inverse of German reunification (case15), where the HIGHEST-P1 state absorbed extreme fusion complexity non-violently. Tests the complexity-capacity thesis at the failure pole: low-P1 fusion -> 1994 civil war -> post-2014 collapse. Safeguard E (oil rents intensifying elite competition).
metadata.notes: Reference-based record; single entity (Yemen). 1990 unification, 1994 civil war (North defeats Southern secession attempt), 2011 uprising, 2014 Houthi takeover of Sana'a, 2015- Saudi-led intervention and de facto territorial breakup. Pre-event proxy: WGI series starts 1996 -> 1990 unavailable, pre scored ~1996 (flagged). MODERATE data (war disrupts series) -> directional-only.

pre_event.event_description: The 1990 fusion of North Yemen (Yemen Arab Republic) and South Yemen (People's Democratic Republic of Yemen) into the Republic of Yemen joined two low-capacity states with rival institutional legacies and competing rent claims. Power-sharing broke down quickly; the 1994 civil war defeated a Southern secession bid and entrenched Northern dominance. Scored at the ~1996 WGI proxy (1990 pre-dates the series).

a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: Yemen consolidates into a stable unified state, OR avoids large-scale violence.

b_violence.prediction: High, ultimately catastrophic violence (1994 civil war, then post-2014 war and humanitarian collapse).

c_convergence.prediction: North-South configuration mismatch never converges; the fused halves diverge back toward de facto separation.
c_convergence.basis: Two rival institutional legacies (tribal-republican North vs Marxist South) joined without the capacity to integrate them; rent competition intensifies the split.

e_fragment_count.prediction: De facto fragmentation (Houthi-controlled north, internationally-recognized-government south, Southern Transitional Council) - a low fragment count that is NOT manageable at floor capacity (Safeguard B).
e_fragment_count.falsification_condition: State stays unified and centrally governed.

g_suppression_mechanism.classification: N/A - fusion / complexity expansion that failed, not a legal-suppression case.

Yemen.outcome_summary: Failed fusion, as predicted. The 1990 union produced the 1994 civil war (defeat of Southern secession), then the 2011 uprising, the 2014 Houthi seizure of Sana'a, and the 2015- Saudi-led war - de facto territorial breakup and one of the world's worst humanitarian crises. P1 collapsed 0.374 -> 0.205 and MI 0.408 -> 0.312 (Tier 3 -> Tier 4); P4 (economic structure) became unscorable amid the war. The inverse of Germany's highest-P1 fusion success (case15).

2015- Saudi-led intervention; de facto territorial breakup (Houthi north / IRG / STC)

analysis.overall_assessment: Clean directional confirmation at the fusion failure pole: 4/4 applicable predictions CONFIRMED (d PARTIAL under the strict re-code). The defining contrast to German reunification (case15).
safeguards_triggered: B (capacity gate: low fragment count unmanageable at floor capacity)
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: Fusion is not inherently stabilizing or destabilizing - the parent capacity decides. Where Germany's highest-P1 base absorbed extreme fusion complexity non-violently (case15), Yemen's low-P1 base, joining two weak rent-competing states, could not integrate the complexity and dissolved violently. The two cases bracket the complexity-capacity thesis for fusion.
analysis.baseline_impact: None; supplies the failed-fusion counterpart to Germany, strengthening the bidirectional fusion reading of the complexity-capacity thesis.
